skills.name: character_body_movement
skills.skill: Implement robust kinematic controller movement for 2D and 3D scenes using CharacterBody2D and CharacterBody3D with move_and_slide.
procedure: Select CharacterBody2D or CharacterBody3D as the root node of the character scene.
Attach a CollisionShape2D/3D with a primitive shape (CapsuleShape or BoxShape).
In GDScript, read directional input inside _physics_process using Input.get_vector or get_axis.
Calculate velocity based on acceleration, friction, and gravity (using ProjectSettings.get_setting('physics/2d/default_gravity') or 3D equivalent).
Assign the calculated Vector2/Vector3 to the velocity property and invoke move_and_slide().
Query collision outcomes via is_on_floor(), is_on_wall(), and get_slide_collision_count() directly after move_and_slide().
verification: Run the scene headless or via debug runner to assert that move_and_slide() executes without warnings.
Verify velocity is properly decelerated by friction when no input is received.
Check that is_on_floor() returns true when colliding with static floor colliders.
pitfalls: Do not pass velocity into move_and_slide() as was done in Godot 3; assign the self.velocity property instead.
Avoid multiplying move_and_slide() velocity by delta; Godot handles time delta internally inside move_and_slide().
Do not modify global_position directly for movement when dynamic collisions are needed, as this bypasses solver iterations.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Create a CharacterBody3D controller in GDScript that implements ground locomotion, gravity, jump mechanics, and returns landing state using is_on_floor().

skills.name: grid_pathfinding_astar
skills.skill: Implement 2D grid-based pathfinding using AStarGrid2D with obstacle avoidance and dynamic updates.
procedure: Instantiate an AStarGrid2D object in script.
Define region boundaries using region = Rect2i(start_x, start_y, width, height) and set cell_size.
Set diagonal_mode (e.g., DIAGONAL_MODE_NEVER or DIAGONAL_MODE_AT_LEAST_ONE_WALKABLE) and heuristic.
Call update() to build the internal grid representation.
Mark obstacles using set_point_solid(grid_pos, true).
Query paths via get_point_path(start_pos, target_pos) or get_id_path() for grid coordinates.
verification: Verify that get_point_path returns a non-empty PackedVector2Array between accessible points.
Verify that setting a cell as solid prevents paths from traversing that cell coordinate.
pitfalls: Failing to call update() after changing grid size or parameters causes pathfinding queries to fail silently or crash.
Passing world positions instead of grid-space Vector2i positions to set_point_solid() or get_id_path().
skills.benchmark_prompt: Construct an AStarGrid2D navigation helper in GDScript that configures a 20x20 grid, sets solid boundaries, and provides a method to get a smoothed world-space Vector2 path.

skills.name: procedural_mesh_generation
skills.skill: Generate runtime dynamic 3D meshes using ArrayMesh and SurfaceTool.
procedure: Instantiate a SurfaceTool instance via SurfaceTool.new().
Call begin(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES) to initialize buffer creation.
Iterate through vertices, emitting set_normal(), set_uv(), and add_vertex() in order per vertex.
Optionally call index() to generate indices or add_index() manually.
Generate tangents using generate_tangents() if normal mapping is required.
Commit the geometry to an ArrayMesh via commit() and assign it to a MeshInstance3D.
verification: Ensure get_surface_count() on the resulting ArrayMesh is greater than zero.
Inspect the generated mesh visually or through automated unit tests checking array sizes in surface_get_arrays().
pitfalls: Attributes like set_color, set_uv, and set_normal must be called *before* add_vertex(); calling them after applies to the subsequent vertex.
Forgetting to call generate_normals() or provide explicit normals results in incorrect lighting artifacts.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Write a GDScript utility class that generates a flat procedural plane mesh of arbitrary width, depth, and subdivision count using SurfaceTool and returns an ArrayMesh.

skills.name: audio_bus_effects_routing
skills.skill: Configure runtime audio buses, adjust volumes, and apply dynamic AudioEffect chains using AudioServer.
procedure: Check or dynamically create an audio bus using AudioServer.add_bus() or AudioServer.get_bus_index(name).
Set bus volume using AudioServer.set_bus_volume_db(bus_idx, linear_to_db(volume)).
Instantiate desired AudioEffect classes (e.g., AudioEffectLowPassFilter, AudioEffectReverb).
Attach the effect to the bus using AudioServer.add_bus_effect(bus_idx, effect, at_position).
Assign AudioStreamPlayer, AudioStreamPlayer2D, or AudioStreamPlayer3D to the target bus via the bus property.
verification: Query AudioServer.get_bus_effect_count(bus_idx) to assert effect presence.
Check AudioServer.is_bus_mute(bus_idx) and ensure output streams are routed correctly without clipping.
pitfalls: Setting volume directly in linear amplitude instead of decibels, which leads to perceived silence or harsh distortion.
Adding duplicate effects on dynamic reloads instead of checking AudioServer.get_bus_effect() first.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Create an AudioController script that initializes an 'Underwater' audio bus routed to 'Master', attaches an AudioEffectLowPassFilter, and toggles filter cutoff frequency via tweening.
